title: Godzilla Stomps Its Way Into MFL Scoring
teaser: "The Cat in the Hat" and Elizabeth Holmes run for their lives.

body.html: Step aside, M. Bison, Other Mommy, and Billy Evans: A new monster has entered the Vulture Movies Fantasy League. Industry veteran Godzilla is back and better than ever, because now he’s earning you MFL points! Also, we’re shouting out some of our favorite team names and taking a look ahead to what’s opening this coming weekend.
Godzilla Plus 60

Back in 2023, we made the mistake of not including Godzilla Minus One among the draftable movies for the Movies Fantasy League. After $57 million in domestic box office and an Oscar win for Best Visual Effects went for naught as far as the MFL was concerned, we were certainly not going to let history repeat itself. You’re welcome, then, to the 4,852 of you who put Godzilla Minus Zero on your team — your ship has come in. Now just be careful Godzilla doesn’t capsize it. Godzilla Minus Zero won the box-office weekend with a $31 million domestic gross, good enough for a +10 bonus for clearing $25 million and a +20 bonus for finishing the weekend at No. 1 — 61 points in all.

Fairly far behind in second place was Warner Bros.’ The Cat in the Hat, which opened to $20 million and no bonus points. While the Dr. Seuss adaptation was never going to come close to the year’s top animated movies like Toy Story 5 or The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, $20 million puts The Cat in the Hat behind the opening-weekend tallies of Hoppers ($45 million), Minion & Monsters ($37 mil), and GOAT ($35 million), and on par with the opening weekend for PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie. Have Thing 1 and Thing 2 lost their drawing power??

In third place: the little-discussed Drummer Boy from Angel Studios. No, it’s not an early Christmas movie. Yes, it’s about the American Revolution. Yes, it stars Jan Levinson-Gould from The Office and Jorah Mormont from Game of Thrones. No, there apparently isn’t any swearing. A $9 million opening weekend is pretty okay for a movie that cost you $3 to add to your roster. It’s a similar story for the Hindi-language Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also a $3 MFL buy, which landed in fifth place on the weekend with an $8 million opening.

Meanwhile, chilling in fourth place is the top-performing movie in the MFL so far, You Can See Everything. With another $8 million added over the weekend, the documentary-ish film is up to $79 million domestic, earning another 15 bonus points for clearing the $75 million threshold. It now extends its lead in the overall MFL standings with 144 points to date.

Other debuts this weekend: Oscar contender Wild Horse Nine picked up $6 million on 1,100 screens, and the “Archie from Riverdale plays Jimmy Stewart, with the voice and everything” biopic Jimmy eked out $2 million. A few other award contenders opened on fewer than ten screens apiece, so both Club Kid and I Play Rocky will have to wait a bit longer for their box-office totals to surpass $1 million.
Name ’Em

One of the best things about a new season of the Movies Fantasy League is another batch of team names that you all came up with. There are always too many funny, clever, insane ones to include, but I combed through the upper echelons of the overall leaderboard to pick out a handful of my faves so far.
In the category of Outstanding Simple Punnery, I’m loving team “Hokum All Ye Faithful.” Simple, effective, ready for the upcoming holiday season.

In the category of Outstanding Complex Punnery, Dual Level, I’m giving it up to team “Tender Loving Carrie Bradshaw,” which works on a few levels, not least of which is making me imagine how Sarah Jessica Parker might have fared in a Mike Leigh movie. But there’s also the patent absurdity of the sentiment itself: a tender, loving Carrie Bradshaw? Can’t imagine it!

In the category of Outstanding Timely Reference, there’s no better choice than team “Elizabeth Holmes a woman first first woman.” Not being able to use punctuation gives some of these thinker team names the aura of a stream-of-consciousness runaway train of an idea. It takes you a second to get to the Veep reference, but once you do, it’s so, so good.
Outstanding Slightly Less Timely Reference goes to team “Trojan Horse Would Have Been Stinky.” Okay, Neil deGrasse Tyson, we found your team.

Outstanding For Your Consideration Advocacy goes to the team named “Boostersbettergetcostume,” a passionate call for Boots Riley’s latest film, I Love Boosters, to get the consideration it deserves in the craft categories. Couldn’t agree more!

Outstanding Achievement in Chain-Reaction Naming recognizes one of the more tried-and-true team-naming formats: the daisy chain of multiple movie titles. “National Treasure Planet of the Apes,” that kind of thing. The team that got named “The Invite to the Debut of The Drama in Primetime” opted against punning and instead linked four buzzy titles into a phrase that scans perfectly. Yes, I would like an invite to the debut of The Drama in prime time, thank you!

But the best name I’ve seen so far, the one that hits me most directly in my movie-nerd sweet spot, is the Michael Clayton–spoofing “im not the cellist u kill im the cellist u buy.” Tony Gilroy is back directing features again with Behemoth!, and in a fit of inspiration, this person pulled out the best quote from George Clooney as the titular Michael Clayton and mashed it up with Pedro Pascal’s ace cellist from Behemoth!. It’s so perfect it doesn’t even need apostrophes.

title: Believe It or Not, "You Can See Everything" Leads All Films in MFL Scoring

body.html: Someone get Billy back from his cousin’s event — there’s big news: You Can See Everything is now the highest-scoring film in the Movies Fantasy League so far. Also in this issue, a bunch of movies get on the board with their first points of the season and we’re gonna break down the best-scoring and best-value movies of the year so far (hint: 👆).
Who’s in First?

In its third week of release, You Can See Everything reached the top of two very important charts. The A24 film — in which Nathan Fielder embeds himself with Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks before she goes to prison and begins to dismantle all our notions of truth, objectivity, performance, and manipulation — finished first place at the weekend box office, edging past Clayface’s showing in its second weekend. It has now climbed up to $63 million total and boasts the best per-screen average of any film in the top 20. With the 20 bonus points that come with finishing first on the weekend, You Can See Everything surged past Verity as the top points earner in the season to date.

Clayface moved up to $44 million total after two weeks, while Street Fighter finished fifth on the weekend, though in advancing to $53 million cumulative, it did earn the 15-point bonus for clearing $50 million. Both Clayface and Street Fighter dropped more than 55 percent from the previous weekend’s take. Wildwood (third place on the weekend and $25 million after two weeks) and Wicker (fourth place on the weekend and $13 million after two weeks) held up better with weekend-to-weekend drops of 39 percent and 28 percent, respectively.

Elsewhere on the charts, a handful of limited-release movies crested over the $1 million mark to earn their first box-office points of the season. Everest: The Other Side, the filmed-in-Imax mountain-climbing documentary from the directors of Free Solo, opened to $1 million, while Cannes Film Festival favorites Fjord and La Bola Negra also crossed that threshold. Netflix is distributing La Bola Negra and granting the film the longest theatrical engagement for any of the streamer’s releases to date, so it’ll be interesting to see how high that number climbs. It’s still only playing on 38 screens.
Other films crossing the $1 million mark include the Alden Ehrenreich–Helen Mirren literary thriller A Talent for Murder and the Taika Waititi–directed floperooni Klara and the Sun.
Leaderboard
After five weeks, a rather fascinating picture has emerged at the top of the movies leaderboard. Based on box-office and Gotham Awards points, we have:

1. You Can See Everything - 128 points
2. Verity - 119 points
3. Other Mommy - 100 points
4. Street Fighter - 98 points
5. Clayface - 74 points
6. The Invite - 50 points
7. All of a Sudden - 50 points
8. Tender Loving Care - 50 points
9. Clarissa - 50 points
10. Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma - 45 points

Perhaps even more interesting is the list of the five best-scoring movies on a points-per-dollar basis, where the total points are divided by how much you paid to draft them. Here’s where You Can See Everything, which only cost $3 to draft, is really dominating the charts and will likely continue to do so all season. (For comparison’s sake, last year’s points-per-dollar champion — Lurker — scored 130 ppd, and I’d expect You Can See Everything to do much better in both awards and box office than Lurker ever did.)

1. You Can See Everything - 42.7 points per dollar
2. Verity - 14.9 points per dollar
3. La Gradiva - 13.3 points per dollar
4. Other Mommy - 12.5 points per dollar
5. Street Fighter - 12.3 points per dollar

title: The MFL Goes to Gotham As Awards Season Kicks Off
teaser: Plus ‘You Can See Everything’ continues to rack up box-office points.

body.html: The calendar may still say “October,” but certain eager awards-giving organizations have reached the end of the year already. The Gotham Awards nominations are out, showering a ton of MFL movies with points and getting lots of players onto the leaderboard for the first time. Plus a box-office update puts new releases Clayface, Wildwood, and Wicker on the board, though You Can See Everything remains the biggest story happening in movie theaters right now.
Awards Season Kicks Off in Gotham

The Gotham Awards announced their nominees on Tuesday morning, bestowing nominations on 35 MFL-eligible films. Perhaps unsurprisingly in the first Gotham Awards of the Zohran Mamdani era, the nominating committees distributed the wealth, awarding nominations to a wide swath of films. The five most nominated were Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s All of a Sudden, Olivia Wilde’s The Invite, Arie and Chuko Esiri’s Clarissa, Mike Leigh’s Tender Loving Care, and Marine Atlan’s La Gradiva. The MFL’s point distribution gave 15 points apiece for nominations in Best Feature, Best Director, Best Lead Performance, and Best Supporting Performance; all other nominations were worth 10 points. That all added up to 50-point totals for All of a Sudden, The Invite, Clarissa, and Tender Loving Care (La Gradiva clocked in close behind with 40 points).

While it’s debatable how much influence the Gotham nominations have over the long-haul race toward the Oscars in March, it’s worth noting that 10 of the 20 lead and supporting performances nominated at the Gothams last year went on to be Oscar-nominated. That’s good news for expected Oscar contenders like Julianne Moore (The Debut), Andrew Scott (Elsinore), John Malkovich (Wild Horse Nine), Penélope Cruz (The Invite), Andrew Garfield (Primetime), and Kate O’Flynn (Tender Loving Care), and encouraging news for more long-shot hopefuls like Mahershala Ali (Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother), Jeon Do-yeon (Possible Love), and Skyler Gisondo (Primetime).

A handful of movies that were drafted on the hopes that they might crash some of the indie awards broke through today, including La Gradiva (Best International Feature, Original Screenplay, Breakthrough Director, and Breakthrough Performance), Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma (Best Feature, Best Director — Jane Schoenbrun, and Best Lead Performance — Gillian Anderson), and Josephine (Best Feature, Best Supporting Performance, and Breakthrough Performance).

While traditionally the Gothams have been awarded to independent and small-budget films, the organization has in recent years unbound itself from such strictures. (The word “independent” didn’t appear in the Gothams’ press release announcing the nominees.) This has opened up the door for some of the films nominated in the Gothams’ Audience Award category, like Project Hail Mary and Michael. (Despite the name, the “Audience Award” will be voted on by Gotham members.)

Box-Office Update

Meanwhile, it was a rather disappointing weekend at the top of the box-office charts. All the goopy eye skin in the world couldn’t help Clayface put together a better opening weekend than a $24 million debut. Still, it was good enough to score the bonus points for finishing the weekend at No. 1. Laika animation studio’s latest film, the visually dazzling and surprisingly violent Wildwood, opened to $12 million. But easily, the story at the box office remains You Can See Everything, which pulled in another $19 million over the weekend, pushing its cumulative total to $45 million. Meanwhile, on only 1,400 screens, Wicker, the movie about having sex with a wicker man, debuted to $5 million. That’s about what The Social Reckoning, the movie about how Facebook destroyed democracy, made on its opening weekend. Extrapolate what you will about the American moviegoing public from that observation.
The other bit of box-office news is that the Gaza war documentary NAZA crossed the $1 million mark this weekend, which, combined with its Gotham nomination, was good for 11 MFL points on the weekend.

title: You Can See Everything's MFL Journey Begins …
teaser: Plus a closer look at the Letterboxd league.

body.html: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s You Can See Everything is the talk of the town. (Well, maybe not every town. In Buffalo, we’re all talking about this stupid-good Josh Allen flick touchdown pass.) But in most places, it’s all about Fielder, Elizabeth Holmes, her sniffly husband, and that mid-movie shift that takes the movie to a higher plane. But did You Can See Everything similarly take its MFL partisans to a higher plane on the leaderboard? Is Verity still the most valuable film on anyone’s roster? And what about this Letterboxd league you keep hearing about?
Box-Office Update

From all the chatter, you’d think You Can See Everything had dominated the box-office charts. But the weekend’s winner was actually Street Fighter, which opened to $31 million. Factoring in the ten bonus points for clearing $20 million and the extra 20 points for topping the weekend box office, Street Fighter kicks off its MFL campaign with 61 points. But the story here really is You Can See Everything, which debuted to $15 million dollars. It was the best opening for a documentary in 13 years (since the One Direction concert movie This Is Us), the biggest opening weekend on fewer than 1,000 screens in 20 years (since Borat), and A24’s fifth-best opening weekend of all time, ranking behind Backrooms, Civil War, Primetime, and Marty Supreme. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s film is already overperforming its $3 price tag and looks poised to be one of the best-value movies of the MFL season.

Elsewhere, Verity continues to be the biggest box-office hit and points-earner of the month, extending its domestic grosses this week to $66 million and its MFL points haul to 111. Other Mommy, which finished third at the box office in its second weekend, is up to $44 million domestic and 74 MFL points.

Opening to a more disappointing total this weekend was 20th Century Studios’ Whalefall, which couldn’t capitalize on Austin Abrams’s recent Resident Evil success — or at least not enough to get people out to watch him get swallowed by a whale. That movie only pulled in $8 million — half of You Can See Everything’s total, despite playing on three times as many screens. Also mired in single digits was Focus Features’ Sense and Sensibility, which totaled $7 million in its opening weekend.

Finally, Digger and The Social Reckoning both continued to sink like a pair of wealthy, isolated stones. Digger finished in 15th place on the weekend, nudging its overall box-office total to $17 million. The Social Reckoning was only slightly better, finishing in 13th and upping its cumulative total to $8 million. Both finished behind the new 4K theatrical release of Ken Russell’s The Devils.
Letterboxd Logs

Now that we’re up and running, I thought we’d take a peek at the brand-new Letterboxd mini-league. We currently have 5,787 players signed up for the Letterboxd league, or about 19 percent of the over 30,000 total people playing the game. Congrats to our current top five:

Lcalderonn: 253 points
Sledging: 246
Lana Del SLAY: 246
Mike R: 215
SkateMckinnon: 210
The current top-scoring players in the Letterboxd league — as well as in the MFL as a whole — are there thanks to some combination of Verity, Street Fighter, and Other Mommy.

Overall, looking at some of the trends, the Letterboxd leaguers had a few films they zeroed in on at a higher rate than the general populace. Those films include Dune: Part Three, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Avengers: Doomsday, and The Invite. That’s right, the Letterboxd league said “Support theatrical distribution!” Of course, they were less bullish than other players on films like The Odyssey, You Can See Everything, and La Bola Negra, so their support for theatrical distribution is, at best, muddled.
Leaderboard

After a five-team pile-up at the top of the overall leaderboard last week, we have some separation this time around. So congrats are in order to new first-place team Box Office Dementus (286 points) for breaking from the pack, thanks to the box-office points for Whalefall and Sense and Sensibility. A perfect example of how movies that don’t win the week can still have a big impact.

Trailing behind in second and third place — and separated by only one point — are the promotionally named “Terrestrial In Theaters Oct 23” (279 points) and the more pun-focused “Godylla Minus Zero” (278 points). Rounding out the top five are teams Ford Prefect and jobifresh, both tied with 263.
Gear Up for the Gothams

The Gotham Award nominations come out next Tuesday. As a result, we’ll be sending out the newsletter a day later than usual so we can include those score updates. And remind any friends who haven’t signed up yet that once a movie earns awards points, it’s ineligible to select for a team, even if it hasn’t opened. So if they’re procrastinating but still plan to pick a team that includes the likes of critical darlings like The Debut or Artificial, they should probably get a move on.

title: Enjoy This Moment, 'Other Mommy' Drafters
teaser: Plus which five squads have a “perfect” score over two weeks?

body.html: Two weeks into Movies Fantasy League scoring, and only four movies have produced points. This has resulted in a kind of glass-half-full/glass-half-empty scenario for approaching your scores at the moment. If you’re sitting at zero points, that’s maybe not so bad, considering the underwhelming debuts so far for movies like Digger. If you drafted box-office winners Verity or Other Mommy, enjoy this time in the sun.
Box Office Update

Jessica Chastain’s new horror movie, Other Mommy, managed to battle back the terrible reviews to take the top spot at the weekend box office. But the film’s $27 million haul wasn’t terribly impressive. It was the lowest opening-weekend tally to top the box-office charts since Send Help and Mercy in the traditionally fallow early months of the year. MFL players hoping that Other Mommy might become a spooky-season hit are probably not going to be thrilled with this. Still, Other Mommy did manage to pick up the ten bonus points for crossing the $25 million threshold and the 20 bonus points for winning the weekend box office for a 57-point debut.

Meanwhile, last weekend’s winner, Verity, upped its box-office total to $53 million, which puts it at 98 MFL points; it leads the league after two weeks. The only other movies to earn enough to accrue box-office points have been Digger (14 points for the film’s $14 million earnings through two weeks) and The Social Reckoning, which opened with a decidedly un-disruptive $5 million.

There are also a handful of MFL movies that opened in limited release — in some cases extremely limited release — but have yet to crest the $1 million threshold. But keep an eye on the “bombshell” documentary NAZA ($298,000 on 85 screens), the Cannes Palme d’Or winner Fjord ($124,000 on four screens), the Chris Rock–directed Misty Green ($85,000 on six screens), and Alex Gibney’s three-hour Elon Musk documentary, titled Musk, which brought in $68,000 on six screens.
Leaderboard

There are currently five teams tied at the top of the overall MFL standings with 174 points apiece. That score represents the highest anyone can manage thus far, meaning these five teams picked Verity, Digger, Other Mommy, and The Social Reckoning, i.e., the only four movies to have scored points. In a way, these five rosters are currently perfect. I just don’t think they’re going to stay that way for long.
Still! Kudos are in order for teams Christian Cerullo, Godylla Minus Zero, mvclarke294, Box Office Dementus, and Terrestrial In Theaters Oct 23 for their momentary top placement.
